Plot a compositional lasso

Source: R/coda_lasso.r
plot.ecodive_coda_lasso.Rd

type = 'signature' draws coda4microbiome's two standard figures side by side: the selected features' coefficients as bars (numerator, positive, in red; denominator, negative, in blue), and the signature score (the linear predictor) by outcome: a box per class for binomial y, against the observed value for gaussian y. type = 'path' draws the coefficients along the \(\lambda\) path, and type = 'cv' the cross-validated error with its standard errors; both mark the chosen \(\lambda\).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_coda_lasso'
plot(x, type = c("signature", "path", "cv"), n_features = 30, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_coda_lasso_pairwise'
plot(x, type = c("signature", "path", "cv"), n_features = 30, ...)

Arguments

x

The result of coda_lasso() or coda_lasso_pairwise().

type

'signature', 'path' or 'cv'. Default: 'signature'

n_features

The most features to show in the signature's bars (the largest \(|\beta|\)). Default: 30

...

Passed to the plotting functions (main, xlab, col, ...).

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

coda4microbiome rescales the coefficients to \(\sum|\beta| = 2\) before drawing them; that changes neither their signs nor their order.

Examples

    set.seed(1)
    counts <- matrix(rpois(240, 50), 30, 8, dimnames = list(NULL, LETTERS[1:8]))
    y      <- log(counts[, 'A'] / counts[, 'B']) + rnorm(30, sd = 0.1)
    fit    <- coda_lasso(counts, y, n_folds = 5, cpus = 1)
    plot(fit)

    plot(fit, type = 'path')

    plot(fit, type = 'cv')
